title: Cap. V Obj. 7 Sol close: Augustine on perseverance; God requires faith then gifts it to the elect
pass_a_gloss: Augustine could find no contradiction here, who best knew that this is the doctrine of the Gospel, Whoever shall have persevered even to the end will be saved; and yet he himself taught that to the saints predestinated into the kingdom of God before the foundations of the world were laid, this very perseverance was prepared and gifted. That I may finish briefly; There is no fight in these two sayings, God first exacts from us the duties of faith, then promises the benefit of life: and God, since for his special mercy he has elected certain ones to share in the benefit of eternal life, therefore wills to give them faith efficaciously, that they may fulfill this duty.
pass_b_english: Augustine found no contradiction here — he knew best that Gospel doctrine is Whoever perseveres to the end will be saved, yet taught that to saints predestinated into God's kingdom before the world's foundations this very perseverance was prepared and gifted. Briefly: these two sayings do not fight — God first exacts from us the duties of faith, then promises the benefit of life; and because for his special mercy he elected certain ones to share eternal life's benefit, he therefore wills to give them faith efficaciously so they may fulfill that duty.
source_text: Nullam hic contradictionem invenire potuit Augustinus, qui optime novit hanc esse Evangelii doctrinam, Quisquis ad finem usque perseveraverit, salvus erit; et tamen ipse docuit, Sanctis in regnum Dei ante jacta mundi fundamenta praedestinatis hanc ipsam perseverantiam praeparatam et donatam. Ut brevi absolvam; Nulla in hisce duobus effatis pugna est, Deus primo a nobis exigit officia fidei, deinde promittit beneficium vitae: et Deus, quoniam pro speciali sua misericordia quosdam elegit ad participandum vitae aeternae beneficium, propterea vult illis efficaciter fidem dare, ut impleant hoc officium.
